info.name: PMP API (v1)
info.description:
Every endpoint of the Performance Management Platform API. Works on any server: the collection's Variables tab holds the server (baseUrl), four test accounts and an extra employee, set for the local demo seed. No environment is needed; see API-GUIDE.md section 1 for what the variables must be on another server.

Folders 00, 01, 02 and 11 only read. Folders 03 to 10 change data: they create and activate a cycle (which can't be undone), and folders 07 and 09 need the server's test clock moved, which affects everyone on that server.

item.name: 00 Auth
item.description: Log in as the four test accounts from the environment and keep their tokens. Every other request uses one of them. Logins are rate-limited to 10 a minute per IP. The first request also computes the run's dates.

exec: pm.test("is an Admin", function () { pm.expect(json.user.roles.admin === true).to.be.true; });
pm.test("is a manager", function () { pm.expect(json.user.roles.manager === true).to.be.true; });
pm.test("is not an Admin (plans would be Admin-authored)", function () { pm.expect(json.user.roles.admin === false).to.be.true; });
pm.test("is not an Admin", function () { pm.expect(json.user.roles.admin === false).to.be.true; });
pm.test("is not an Admin", function () { pm.expect(json.user.roles.admin === false).to.be.true; });

item.name: 01 Read-only (safe on any server)
item.description: GET requests that change nothing. Run 00 Auth, this folder and 11 Logout to smoke-test a server such as UAT without touching its data.

exec: pm.test("at least one category (plans need one)", function () { pm.expect(json.data.length > 0).to.be.true; });
pm.test("status is one of [403, 404]", function () { pm.expect([403, 404].includes(pm.response.code)).to.be.true; });

item.name: Issues of the latest run (filter by type)
02 Check the test accounts
item.description: Read-only checks that the accounts and the extra employee fit the scenario. Fix the environment if one fails; the folders after this one change data.

exec: pm.test("line manager is the manager account", function () { pm.expect(json.data.line_manager_id === Number(pm.variables.get('managerEmployeeId'))).to.be.true; });
pm.test("line manager is the manager account", function () { pm.expect(json.data.line_manager_id === Number(pm.variables.get('managerEmployeeId'))).to.be.true; });

item.name: Find the extra employee by code

exec: pm.test("not one of the test employees", function () { pm.expect(![pm.variables.get('employeeEmployeeId'), pm.variables.get('employee2EmployeeId')].map(Number).includes(json.data[0].id)).to.be.true; });

item.name: 03 Configuration (Admin)
item.description: Policy, competency templates, objective categories and email templates. Leaves the configuration as it found it: the policy is re-published unchanged (a new version with the same values), and the template, category and email-template change made here are undone.

exec: pm.collectionVariables.set("policyLevelsJson", JSON.stringify(json.data.levels.map(l => ({level: l.level, label: l.label, threshold_bp: l.threshold_bp, bell_min_bp: l.bell_min_bp, bell_max_bp: l.bell_max_bp}))));
pm.collectionVariables.set("policyBellJson", JSON.stringify(json.data.levels.map(l => ({level: l.level, bell_min_bp: l.bell_min_bp, bell_max_bp: l.bell_max_bp}))));

item.name: Preview Bell Curve head counts (unsaved limits)
Publish a new policy version (same values)
Attach job titles to the template

request.description: Example body: {"job_title_ids": [17]}. The run attaches a job title only when one has no template, and releases it again in the next request.

item.name: Delete the template (releases its job titles)
04 Eligibility (Admin)
item.description: Creates an inactive exclusion rule and deletes it again, so nobody's eligibility changes.

item.name: 05 Cycles (Admin)
item.description: A sandbox draft shows the draft lifecycle and is deleted. The main cycle is scoped to the two test employees and the extra employee, and activated. Activation can't be undone: the cycle stays on the server (it is named "API test cycle" with the run tag).

item.name: Change the draft (deadlines may be partial)

exec: pm.test("all three included", function () { pm.expect([pm.variables.get('employeeEmployeeId'), pm.variables.get('employee2EmployeeId'), pm.variables.get('extraEmployeeId')].map(Number).every(id => json.data.candidates.some(c => c.employee_id === id && c.status === 'included'))).to.be.true; });
pm.test("manager in the new cycle", function () { pm.expect(json.data.some(c => c.id === Number(pm.variables.get('cycleId')) && c.my_roles.manager)).to.be.true; });

pm.test("both test employees listed", function () { pm.expect([pm.variables.get('memberAId'), pm.variables.get('memberBId')].map(Number).every(id => json.data.some(r => r.cycle_member_id === id))).to.be.true; });

item.name: 06 Plans
item.description: Goal Setting. Plan A (employee) is written by the manager and goes through every workflow action. Plan B (employee 2) is written by Admin and goes straight to the employee. Plan C (the extra member) is created and deleted, and the extra member is removed from the cycle. Every write sends the plan's current `version`; the test scripts keep it up to date.

item.name: Second plan for the same member (409)

exec: pm.test("version conflict", function () { pm.expect(json.error.code === 'conflict' && 'current_version' in json.error.details).to.be.true; });

item.name: Manager submits plan A to Admin
Admin returns plan A with comments
Manager edits plan A (rows kept by id)
Admin approves plan A (goes to the employee)

exec: pm.test("straight back to the employee", function () { pm.expect(json.data.status === 'pending_employee').to.be.true; });

item.name: Employee requests a modification (2nd: flags Admin)
Plan A history (Admin sees internal events)
Admin submits plan B (straight to the employee)
Remove the extra member (reason as query)

url.raw: {{baseUrl}}/api/v1/admin/cycles/{{cycleId}}/members/{{extraEmployeeId}}?reason=Moved to a project outside the cycle scope.

query.value: Moved to a project outside the cycle scope.

item.name: 07 Evaluation (Manager Evaluation stage)
item.description:
Terminal step before this folder: on the server, move the test clock into Manager Evaluation, past the Active Performance deadline:

    php artisan pmp:clock --advance="222 days"

This moves the clock for every user and cycle on that server.

Then the manager enters actuals, competency ratings (whatever competencies the employee's template has) and evidence. Plan A gets every rating at 4, plan B at 3; on the demo policy that is 92.2% (level 4) and about 80% (level 3).

item.name: Save part of plan A (one actual)

exec: pm.test("not complete yet", function () { pm.expect(json.data.is_complete === false && json.data.rating === null).to.be.true; });

item.name: Complete plan A (rest of actuals and ratings)

request.description: Example body: {"version": 1, "kpis": [{"plan_kpi_id": 2, "actual": 10}], "competencies": [{"competency_id": 5, "rating": 4}, {"competency_id": 6, "rating": 4}]}. The run sends a rating for every competency of the template.

exec: pm.test("complete with a rating", function () { pm.expect(json.data.is_complete === true && json.data.rating !== null).to.be.true; });

request.description: In Postman, pick sample-evidence.pdf (next to the collection) as the file if it isn't found.

item.name: Complete plan B in one save

exec: pm.test("complete with a rating", function () { pm.expect(json.data.is_complete === true && json.data.rating !== null).to.be.true; });

item.name: 08 Groups and final review
item.description: The manager submits the team as one group; Admin returns it once, the manager fixes an evaluation and resubmits, and Admin approves. Approve and return send the group's `expected_version`. If the server's Bell Curve doesn't allow the two ratings for a group of 2, the submit fails with the blockers in the response.

exec: pm.test("can submit (otherwise see blockers)", function () { pm.expect(json.data.can_submit === true).to.be.true; });

item.name: Saving after submit is refused (422 evaluation_locked)
Fix plan B after the return
Results before publication (Admin sees published: false)

exec: pm.test("two unpublished results", function () { pm.expect(json.data.length === 2 && json.data.every(r => r.published === false)).to.be.true; });

item.name: 09 Results (after publication)
item.description:
Terminal step before this folder: on the server, move the clock past the Admin Final Review deadline, which publishes approved groups:

    php artisan pmp:clock --advance="93 days"

After the run, put the clock back with `php artisan pmp:clock --reset`.

exec: pm.test("published result for this cycle", function () { pm.expect(json.data.some(r => (r => r.cycle.id === Number(pm.variables.get('cycleId')))(r) && r.published === true)).to.be.true; });

item.name: 10 Admin grants
item.description: Grants the Admin role to employee 2 and takes it away again. Skipped when employee 2 is already an Admin, so no real Admin loses the role.

11 Logout
item.description: Revoke every token taken in 00 Auth.
